title: Osage Orange: Old Osage Orange Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Every autumn it drops green spheres the size of a grapefruit that nothing alive wants to eat. Four osage oranges mapped in European parks.
intro: Every autumn these trees drop green spheres the size of a grapefruit that nothing alive wants to eat. The fruit of Maclura pomifera looks like a brain, weighs a kilo or more and seems to have been built for animals that vanished from North America thousands of years ago. The tree takes its name from the Osage nation, who made bows from the wood, which is dense and springy and was traded far beyond their own territory. American farmers then found a second use: planted close and cut back, osage orange grows into a thorn hedge nothing can push through, and thousands of miles of it went in through the 1850s until barbed wire made it pointless. All four here are curiosities in European parks, two in Barcelona and one each in Lyon and Toulouse. Stand under one in November and watch your head.
